title: AI Art and DMCA
author: iMikeLi
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/7koadx3a0coh1.png?width=777&format=png&auto=webp&s=6d6433230015c8b617c35961979c91036655a809

Hey everyone,

I’ve been developing my indie game solo for about a year now. I taught myself programming and I’m currently studying CS, but visual art has always been my weakest point by far. As a student, hiring 3D or 2D concept artists is completely out of my budget, so I’ve been leaning heavily on AI tools (image generation, img-to-3D workflows, etc.) to get workable assets into my engine.

Recently, I ran a quick check on a design reference I was exploring—and as you can see in the screenshot, Google’s reverse search instantly pinned it down: *Aging Untouchable* from *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* (Bandai Namco / FromSoftware IP).

That was a bit of a wake-up call regarding DMCA risks. It got me wondering how other solo devs without an art background navigate this safely?

I’m trying to establish a reliable, legally clean pipeline that lets me produce dark fantasy assets without accidentally copying FromSoftware’s homework. Any advice or workflows would be appreciated!

comments.author: Upstairs_West6628
comments.body: Brother that isn’t an aging untouchable, the only resemblance is the big orange ball, but other than that, none. There is no way the AI is right on this. So i guess that muddies up your question even more.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Don't ask AI for legal advice, AI detection, art attribution, or anything like that. AI hallucinates a lot. AI image recognition doesn't works like ours. They get a JSON with a text description of all the elements on a picture and guessing what is this. 

As for, how do you know if it's plagiary or not. I think there's plenty of tree men with glowing yelow head on a market. Just look how good Chinese businesses at making knock offs. Their changes are very subtle and yet they're allowed on a world market. your tree person is far enough
